mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.1% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days across all monetary regimes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 8.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 8.0%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate weakening consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of cases, or the interaction term's coefficient is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on the interaction of HOUST and RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, declining industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to anticipated earnings slowdowns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods during late-cycle expansion when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2.0% indicates robust economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in all demand regimes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 225.0 indicates persistent price pressures, triggering monetary policy tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 225.0, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong non-farm payrolls growth (PAYEMS) above 100 (thousand persons) indicates a robust labor market, supporting consumer spending and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days across all labor regimes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 100, or the Rank IC is below 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in FEDFUNDS and rise in CPIAUCSL indicates monetary policy response to inflation, creating uncertainty that drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of FEDFUNDS decline and CPIAUCSL rise fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of cases, or the interaction term's coefficient is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on the interaction of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL.
